definition: A loss function commonly used for classification tasks that measures the difference between predicted and true probability distributions.
details: Cross-entropy loss is the standard training objective for next-token prediction in language models, where the model predicts a probability distribution over the vocabulary at each step.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Cross-Entropy Loss — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
